body:
N-26 SLICE 1 IS BUILT, NOT WALKED, NOT MARKED (helper-n26, 14 Nov 2026; PR #78). The item is NOT complete: RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md 4b needs slices 1 AND 2 in the first public image, so I did not run `roadmap.py mark`. Slice 2 is not opened.

WHAT SLICE 1 DOES: imports/uploads.py is the one door (read_declared / read_official_video / read_upload); readers._read_entry gates on videoType (ATV, OFFICIAL_SOURCE_MUSIC and removed entries declared; OMV read_official_video; UGC, any unknown value, an available entry with no videoType and no album = an upload); the yt-dlp reader calls read_upload. Whole-name Unicode channel test (never a substring), every dash + middle dot + bullet, brackets never decide. Track carries artist_basis and uploader IN MEMORY ONLY. Proof: tests/test_import_upload_reading.py on 9 recorded YouTube Music search answers (tests/fixtures/ytm/n26; the playlist shape is constructed), the invariance tests (all recorded playlists, all 60 recorded credited OMVs), 12 mutation checks.

FOR SLICE 2:
1. Persist artist_basis on the ref, INCLUDING the fourth basis `unknown`: a song nobody names (recorded OMV `Akudama`, empty artists; a Spotify track may list none) has artist "" and basis `unknown` in the reader; ImportService._song_of files it under "Unknown Artist" (textnorm.UNKNOWN_ARTIST). Treat `unknown` like `channel` in the all-channel artist-picture rule.
2. THE PLACEHOLDER CARRIES NO IDENTITY (done in slice 1 after review): refs.find never matches a description whose artist is textnorm.is_unknown_artist by artist+title+length (live refs and ref_merge tombstones), only by video id / ISRC / catalogue id; artist_finder._due skips the name, so no catalogue look-up for "Unknown Artist" leaves the Host's address. Cost, accepted: a description with the placeholder and NO id is a new ref each time (an import has its video; the scanner finds a file's ref by the file first); a real artist literally named "Unknown Artist" is treated the same. The N-11 repair merges only refs sharing a file and holds two that name different videos, so it cannot merge two nameless songs.
3. The OMV rule keeps the artist's name in the song title as today ("Metallica - One (Live) [...]"); a later cleanup may strip it.

KNOWN LEFTOVERS (pinned by named tests, all under N-28): an OMV credited to a LABEL with no separator (Pure Noise Records / Vomit Forth) keeps the label; an upload whose title names nobody keeps its uploader flagged `channel` (David C); `Lionel Messi * Monaco - Bad Bunny` is read artist-first (U2); ARTE Concert and Crunchyroll stay under their channels until slice 4. The OMV rule can misread `Song - Subtitle` under a band's credit.

DECISION (yours to overrule): an OMV whose title says the credited name ANYWHERE keeps the credit even when neither side of the separator is that name. Recorded case: `DANDADAN Opening in ITALIANO - EXTENDED "Otonoke" Creepy Nuts | ItsKlyo` is typed OMV, credited to ItsKlyo; read literally the rule made "DANDADAN Opening in ITALIANO" an artist (basis `title`). Cost: a label credit repeated in the title also stays.

HOUSEKEEPING: AUDIT-BUILT had two B-125 and two B-126 rows on main (merge residue of #72/#74); this PR keeps one B-125 row (updated, stays open) and the newest B-126 row (from #77). This note is committed in the slice 1 PR, so it shows on the board when that merges.
